items.title: 0.1.2 spec: key-host wave 2, Tembo, Capy, Ona and OpenComputer drivers
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Four more agent hosts run Claude Code or Codex for their users and can start, wake and stop a run only through an HTTP API that takes the user's key: Tembo, Capy, Ona (formerly Gitpod) and OpenComputer. None can be an OpenWiz host today. The drivers census (private) classes them with OpenHands Cloud and Warp Oz (spec #2425) as key hosts, buildable on spec #2378's key helper.

## Solution

Four new drivers, one per host, each built exactly as #2425's: only on the key helper (driver v1 rule N4, from #2378's KY1), each taking the user's effort or declaring that it can't (J318, #2471's EF1). Each starts a run for a ticket, wakes the same run and stops it, sending every request through the helper to its host's registered address. The key stays in the user's keychain or an environment variable they set. The driver never sees it, and OpenWiz never stores it. A host where waking the same run or stopping it turns out not to work gets no driver. Each driver passes the kit on fixtures in CI, and on the real host in a live check the owner runs.

## Changelog headline

You can now run OpenWiz fleets on Tembo, Capy, Ona and OpenComputer, with your API key kept on your own computer.

## User Stories

1. As a Tembo, Capy, Ona or OpenComputer user, I keep my host's API key in my keychain or an environment variable, and OpenWiz starts, wakes and stops runs for my tickets there.
2. As a user, I choose Claude Code or Codex for the run where the host offers it, and my harness login is never passed by OpenWiz.
3. As a user, I can revoke OpenWiz's access by removing the key, and OpenWiz never stored it.
4. As a reviewer, I trust each driver because the kit proves it never sees the key and only reaches its host's registered address.
5. As the owner, I see each driver pass 5 of 5 on the real host before it merges.

## Implementation Decisions

- **The same shape as #2425.** Each driver calls the kit's key helper with a host name, a method and a path, and never names, reads or passes the key, nor builds an address. It relies on driver v1, the kit's schema, the helper and its registry as #2379 defines them, and on EF1's effort field (#2558). There is no contract-first ticket: the shared interfaces are KY1's and EF1's.
- **One registry row each** in the kit's host registry, shared with #2378's and #2425's tickets: `tembo`, `capy`, `ona` and `opencomputer`, each with its own `<HOST>_API_KEY` variable and `openwiz-<host>` keychain entry.
- **Each host's open question stops its builder** (from the census): Capy, whether cloud threads can use the user's own subscriptions; Ona, whether a finished run can be woken; OpenComputer, its deployed agent definition and uploaded harness token, which OpenWiz must never upload (N2). Tembo has none.
- **Effort (J318):** each driver takes the user's effort or declares none, with the exact refusal text. Never a silent default.
- **Live checks are the owner's.** Each driver merges only after its live check records 5 of 5 on the real host at the build pull request's approved head (driver contract section 3).

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam:** the driver kit (`kit.py`), on fixtures in CI, against a fake host that the helper reaches through its loopback test override. It is the seam #2378's Devin driver and #2425's drivers use.
- **Behaviour to prove:** each driver passes all five checks, its key check included; it fails first against the copied template; no file of the driver names the key's variable or calls the keychain; and nothing it passes or prints carries the key.
- **Prior art:** #2425's drivers (#2429, #2444), #2378's Devin driver (KY2) and the kit's key check (KY1).

## Proof

| Claim | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| P1 Tembo driver passes the kit | The kit on fixtures in CI, red first; the live 5-of-5 run |
| P2 Capy driver passes the kit | The kit on fixtures in CI, red first; the live 5-of-5 run |
| P3 Ona driver passes the kit | The kit on fixtures in CI, red first; the live 5-of-5 run |
| P4 OpenComputer driver passes the kit | The kit on fixtures in CI, red first; the live 5-of-5 run |
| P5 No driver sees the key | The kit's key check, and the code review |

## Checkpoints

- One-way door: no
- User-visible: yes

## Live check

One throwaway ticket per host, on the owner's own account, with the key in the owner's keychain or environment: the kit prints 5 of 5 against the real host at the approved head.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the key helper, its rule, the kit or the effort contract (#2378, #2471).
- The class A and unknown hosts in the census.
- Storing or managing any key.

## Further Notes

From Jake's go (J314), which the planner ruled covers this second wave. Sources: the drivers census (private), specs #2378, #2425 and #2471, and driver v1.

items.title: 0.1.2 spec: the live-check rig, scheduled kit runs and WizMarket receipts
items.body:
## Problem Statement

A driver or harness listing in the marketplace registry (`openwizdev/WizMarket`) may only show `verified` with a receipt of a real 5-of-5 run of driver v1's kit (`kernel/driver-kit/kit.py`). Today nobody produces those receipts. A live check is a person's job: set up a throwaway repository and ticket, run the kit by hand against one host, copy its output into an evidence file and write it up. It has been done once for boat.dev (2 of 5, `adapters/boat/evidence/live-b1423db.txt`) and as a smoke run for Cloudroom (`adapters/cloudroom/evidence/live-smoke.txt`, not a kit run). So no listing can be verified, and a driver that breaks on its real host goes unnoticed until a person looks again.

## Solution

A small **live-check rig** in `kernel/live-rig/` runs the kit against real hosts on a schedule from Jake's PC, wherever a signed-in tool already exists there. Each run leaves a run record. A host whose tool is missing, isn't signed in, or whose run might cost money is skipped, and the record says why. From a 5-of-5 run record, one command writes the receipt in exactly the form WizMarket's listing contract (`contracts/listing.v1.md` in `openwizdev/WizMarket`, its ticket MK1) accepts as proof for a `verified` listing. The first hosts are the three shipped drivers: local, boat.dev and Cloudroom.

**Jake's VPS session (orchestrator's order, 2026-11-22).** Jake's sign-in live checks for the wave-1 drivers waiting on live runs (#1987: Hermes, Pane, Factory, Conductor and Cursor cloud agents) wait for his VPS (arriving 2026-11-23 or 11-24). The rig makes that one short session: a bootstrap installs each host's free tool, one page lists the exact sign-in Jake runs per host and whether a turn bills beyond a plan he already has, and one command runs the five checks for every signed-in host at each build PR's frozen approved head and posts the results in the forms the live-check tickets and WizMarket accept. All of it is rehearsed first in a throwaway cloud sandbox with fake sign-ins.

**Hard limits:** the rig never signs in, never installs anything without Jake's OK, never spends money, never starts a paid run, and never reads, prints or passes a key. The scheduled rig writes nothing to GitHub; only `heads.py --post`, run by a person, posts, through that person's own `gh`.

## Changelog headline

none

## User Stories

1. As Jake, the rig checks my shipped drivers against their real hosts on a schedule, with the tools I've already signed in to, without me starting anything.
2. As Jake, a host whose tool isn't installed or signed in is skipped and recorded as `skipped: <why>`; the rig never asks me to sign in and never installs it.
3. As Jake, a host whose run could cost money is skipped as `skipped: cost`, until I say otherwise in its config.
4. As a listing author, a 5-of-5 run gives me a receipt file in exactly the form WizMarket accepts for `verified`, and nothing else does.
5. As a reviewer, the rig's runner, schedule and receipt writer are tested on fixtures in the cloud, with the kit's own fake harness and fake hosts, never a real one.
6. As the orchestrator (PC hands), one ticket gives me the exact command and schedule to put on the PC.
7. As Jake on my new VPS, one bootstrap installs every waiting host's free tool, with no sign-in and no spend.
8. As Jake, one page tells me, per host, the exact sign-in command I run, the environment names I set myself, and whether a turn bills beyond a plan I already have.
9. As Jake, one command runs the five checks for every host I've signed in to, at each driver PR's frozen approved head, and posts each result on its build PR and each 5-of-5 receipt to WizMarket, only when I pass `--post`.
10. As the orchestrator, the whole session has been rehearsed in a throwaway cloud sandbox before Jake's first run.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Where:** everything lives in `kernel/live-rig/`, standard-library Python 3.9+, Linux and macOS (as the kit). The kit's own files (`kernel/driver-kit/`) belong to KY1 (#2379) and are not touched; the rig runs `kit.py` as a program and reads only its stdout and exit code.
- **Host config,** `kernel/live-rig/hosts/<host>.json`, one per host, plain JSON with exactly these keys:
  - `host`: the real host's name (`local`, `boat.dev`, `Cloudroom`);
  - `driver`: the driver path in this repository, as `adapters/<host>/driver`;
  - `needs`: programs that must be on `PATH` (for example `["boat"]`); one missing gives `skipped: not installed: <program>`;
  - `signed_in`: a list of read-only status commands (argument lists), each of which must exit 0 within 30 seconds, with output discarded; any other answer gives `skipped: not signed in: <program>`. A command that signs in, opens a browser, prompts, or prints a credential is never allowed; each host ticket names its command's source. A probe must also raise no OS prompt (keyring, keychain, browser) and refresh nothing. GitHub's is exactly `env GH_TELEMETRY=0 gh config get -h github.com user` (reads `hosts.yml` only in gh 2.105.0; telemetry off). **Named exception:** Claude Code has no safe unattended sign-in probe (`claude auth status` can enter OAuth refresh and take a refresh lock: openclaw/openclaw#189214 and PR #197032; its macOS store is the Keychain), so a `claude` harness gets `needs` only. A signed-out claude then records as the kit's `fail start`, with no sign-in, prompt or spend, because the drivers' first-turn watch refuses a sign-in line (the planner's decision on #2751);
  - `cost`: `none`, `paid` or `unknown`. Only `none` runs; `paid` and `unknown` give `skipped: cost`. Changing it to `none` needs Jake's recorded OK, named in the config's pull request;
  - `runs`: a list of `{"harness": ..., "model": ...}`, each one kit run;
  - `wait`: the kit's `--wait`, at most 900.
- **Settings outside the repository:** the throwaway repository and ticket the kit uses live in a local settings file the person passes (`--settings <file>`, JSON `{"repo": "<owner>/<name>", "ticket": <n>}`), never in the repository.
- **Runner,** `kernel/live-rig/rig.py`:
  `python3 -I kernel/live-rig/rig.py --hosts kernel/live-rig/hosts --settings <file> --out <dir> [--host <name>]`
  - refuses (exit 2) from a checkout with uncommitted changes, because a receipt must name a real commit;
  - holds one lock in `--out`, so two scheduled runs never overlap; a second run exits 0 with `rig.py: another run holds the lock`;
  - per host: `needs`, then `cost`, then `signed_in` (so a host whose cost isn't `none` never runs a status probe), then each `runs` entry with `python3 -I kernel/driver-kit/kit.py --driver <driver> --repo <repo> --ticket <n> --harness <h> --model <m> --wait <w>`, with the caller's environment unchanged (it never reads, adds or prints a variable's value);
  - writes one run record per entry, `<out>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<host>-<harness>-<model>.json`, then prints one summary line per entry: `ran <host> <harness>: <k> of 5` or `skipped <host> <harness>: <why>`;
  - exit 0 when every entry ran or was skipped; 1 when a run's kit exited 1 or 2; 2 when the rig itself could not run.
- **Run record** (the one interface between the runner and the receipt writer), JSON with exactly: `host`, `harness`, `model`, `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC), `driver_commit` and `kit_commit` (the checkout's 40-hex `HEAD`), `outcome` (`ran` or `skipped`), `skipped` (the reason, or `null`), `kit_exit` (integer or `null`), `stdout` (the kit's stdout verbatim, or `null`), `seconds` (integer wall time). No path, login, repository name or environment value goes in it.
- **Schedule,** `kernel/live-rig/schedule.json`: `{"cron": "0 3 * * 1", "timezone": "<IANA zone>", "command": [...]}`, weekly on Monday 03:00 on the PC. The orchestrator puts it on the PC as a Local Cloudroom loop (or the PC's own scheduler); the cloud never runs it.
- **Receipt writer,** `kernel/live-rig/receipt.py`:
  `python3 -I kernel/live-rig/receipt.py <run record> --listing <id> --run-by <login> -o <dir>`
  writes `receipts/<listing-id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<driver commit, 12 hex>.txt` in exactly WizMarket's `contracts/listing.v1.md` shape (MK1), and only from a run record with `outcome: ran`, `kit_exit: 0` and the five `pass` lines in the order version, start, wake, stop, token. Anything else exits 1 with the reason and writes nothing. Before writing, it runs the kit's credential shapes over the text and refuses on a hit. The header and body are MK1's; this spec doesn't fix a second format. As spec #2476 sets it: `# listing`, `# host`, `# driver: openwizdev/OpenWiz@<40 hex>`, `# kit: openwizdev/OpenWiz@<40 hex>`, `# harness`, `# model`, `# date`, `# run by` (the login whose `gh` the kit read with) header lines, then kit.py's stdout verbatim and `Result: 5 of 5 pass`. The WizMarket pull request that adds a receipt is its public record; the throwaway repository and ticket never appear.
- **Listing ids,** `kernel/live-rig/listings.json`: maps `<host>` (driver listing) and `<host>/<harness>` (harness listing) to MK1's listing ids (spec #2476 names `local`, `boat-dev` and `cloudroom`); owned by the receipt ticket, because MK1 fixes the id form.
- **VPS session files** live in `kernel/live-rig/vps/`.
  - **Bootstrap,** `kernel/live-rig/vps/bootstrap.sh` with `kernel/live-rig/vps/tools.json`: for each host (`hermes`, `pane`, `factory`, `conductor`, `cursor`) the tool it needs (`hermes`; `runpane` and its daemon; `droid`; for the two API hosts, `curl` 8.3 or later only) with its install source, exact version and checksum, plus the shared `git`, `gh` and `python3` 3.9+. The drivers pin no tool versions today, so `tools.json` records the version each driver's README and fixtures were written against where it says one, else the latest stable release on the day the ticket is built, with its source. It installs into the user's own prefix (`~/.local`), never with `sudo` unless Jake runs it so, installs only free CLIs, runs no tool beyond `--version`, never signs in, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` prints the plan and changes nothing.
  - **The page,** `kernel/live-rig/vps/SIGN-IN.md`: the session in order (bootstrap, sign-ins, one command), then one row per host: the exact sign-in command Jake runs (or the dashboard step), the environment variable names he exports himself for the API hosts (`CONDUCTOR_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY`, `FACTORY_API_KEY`; names only, never values), the read-only status command, and whether one live turn **bills beyond a plan he already has** (`no`, `yes` or `unknown`), each with its source. Plus `gh auth login`.
  - **VPS host configs,** `kernel/live-rig/vps/hosts/<host>.json`, in the host config shape above, owned by the page's ticket. Every one of the five bills a turn (their READMEs say so), so each carries `cost: paid`; the command runs one only when Jake passes `--allow-cost <host>` himself.
  - **The frozen-head command,** `kernel/live-rig/heads.py`:
    `python3 -I kernel/live-rig/heads.py --tickets kernel/live-rig/vps/live-tickets.json --hosts kernel/live-rig/vps/hosts --settings <file> --out <dir> [--allow-cost <host>]... [--post]`
    - `kernel/live-rig/vps/live-tickets.json` maps each host to its live-check ticket (DW1L #1990 Hermes, DW3L #1993 Conductor, DW4L #1995 Cursor, DW6L #1999 Factory, DW7L #2001 Pane), its build PR and its WizMarket listing id;
    - reads each live-check ticket's latest `launch-fleet: look: live run due at the approved frozen head of #<PR>: <40 hex>` line (one REST read per ticket, with a saved ETag); no line is `skipped: no frozen head`;
    - checks each host with `rig.py`'s `load_host` and `check_host`, then `cost` against `--allow-cost`;
    - fetches the head with `git fetch origin <sha>` into its own worktree, refuses if the fetched commit isn't exactly the line's, and runs this checkout's `kernel/driver-kit/kit.py` with `--driver <worktree>/adapters/<host>/driver`; it writes a run record in the spec's shape, with `driver_commit` the frozen head and `kit_commit` this checkout's `HEAD`;
    - writes, for each run, the build-PR comment in the KN form, `**<ID> live kit run: <k> of 5 pass**, at head \`<40 hex>\`` then the kit's lines in a code block and nothing private, and for each 5-of-5 the WizMarket receipt through `receipt.py`;
    - posts only with `--post`, through the person's own signed-in `gh`: one comment per run on the build PR, and one WizMarket pull request with that run's receipts. Without `--post` it prints what it would post. An agent never passes `--post` or `--allow-cost` outside a fixture.
  - **The rehearsal:** a fresh child in its own throwaway cloud sandbox runs the whole session from a clean clone: the real bootstrap (free CLIs only), fake sign-ins (fake status commands first on `PATH`; no real sign-in), and `heads.py` against each driver's own `fixtures/bin` fakes and a fixture ticket file, with agent-CLI refusal stubs first on `PATH` wherever no fake is wired; it never passes `--post` to GitHub (a fixture `gh`) and never runs on the PC.
- **Contract-first:**- **Contract-first:** the receipt's contract is MK1's (external blocker); the run record and host config are fixed here, in this spec, so the runner, receipt writer and host configs build in parallel.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seams:** `rig.py`'s command line and run records; `receipt.py`'s command line and the receipt file; each host config through `rig.py`.
- **Prior art:** `kernel/driver-kit/test_kit.py` and its fixtures (`fixtures/fake-harness`, `fixtures/planted/`), and `adapters/*/fixtures/` fake hosts (`adapters/cloudroom/fixtures/room-cli`).
- **Runner tests** (`kernel/live-rig/test_rig.py`), on fixtures only: a fixture host whose driver is `adapters/template/driver` with the fake harness runs 5 of 5 and writes its run record; a missing program, a failing status command and `cost: unknown` each give the exact `skipped` line and record, and start no kit; a dirty checkout exits 2; a held lock exits 0 and runs nothing; a planted driver's failing kit gives exit 1 and `k of 5`; no run record holds a path, a login, the settings' repository, or a planted secret from the environment.
- **VPS tests:** `kernel/live-rig/vps/test_bootstrap.py` runs `bootstrap.sh --dry-run` and a fixture install into a temp prefix with fake installers; `kernel/live-rig/vps/test_hosts.py` checks each VPS host config through `rig.py` and that the page names every host in `tools.json`; `kernel/live-rig/test_heads.py` runs `heads.py` on fixture tickets, a fixture driver, a fake `gh` and a fake `git` remote: no frozen head, a head that doesn't match, a host not signed in, a paid host without `--allow-cost`, 5 of 5 with the exact PR comment and receipt, and `--post` reaching only the fake `gh`.
- **Receipt tests** (`kernel/live-rig/test_receipt.py`): a 5-of-5 record gives a byte-exact expected receipt; 4 of 5, a skipped record, lines out of order and a planted credential each refuse and write nothing; the receipt passes WizMarket's own receipt check, when MK1 ships one.
- **Host config tests:** each host ticket runs `rig.py --host <name>` with fake `needs` programs on `PATH` (signed in, not signed in, missing) and shows each skip line; the real status command is checked against the tool's own docs, never run against a real account in the cloud.
- **CI:** one step under the kernel kits' tests in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (granted to the runner ticket) runs every `kernel/live-rig/test_*.py` and `kernel/live-rig/*/test_*.py` (so `hosts/` and `vps/` too), so later tickets need no CI edit.
- Every suite runs as `env -u OPENWIZ_GITHUB_APP_KEY <command>`.

## Proof

| Claim | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| A signed-in host with free runs gets a run record per harness | `test_rig.py` fixture run, red first (no `rig.py`) |
| A missing, signed-out or possibly paid host is skipped and recorded, and no kit starts | `test_rig.py` skip cases |
| The rig never handles a key | `test_rig.py` planted-secret case; review of `rig.py` |
| A 5-of-5 record gives WizMarket's receipt, and nothing else does | `test_receipt.py` byte-exact and refusal cases, against MK1's contract |
| The three first hosts are configured, with read-only status commands | each host ticket's skip-line runs and the command's cited source |
| Real receipts on the PC | the person's ticket: the first scheduled run's summary lines and any receipts, public summary only |
| The VPS session is one short session, rehearsed | the rehearsal ticket's transcript from a fresh cloud sandbox: bootstrap, fake sign-ins, `heads.py` on fixtures, timed |
| Time and verifiable listings, before and after | BEFORE bench in this spec; the AFTER bench ticket |

## BEFORE bench

| Measure | Today |
| --- | --- |

items.title: 0.1.2 spec: Harness wave 1: nine local agent CLIs as harness rows on the local driver
items.body:
## Problem Statement

The local driver runs only `claude` and `codex`. People run many other agent CLIs that start a headless run, resume it by a session id, and stop when their process ends. The drivers census (private) found nine of them buildable today: Pi, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI (`agent`), Goose, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, Qwen Code and Cline CLI. Each one, copied into its own driver, would repeat the local driver's supervisor, its permission-mode rules and its stop logic nine times.

## Solution

Each of the nine CLIs becomes one **harness row** on the one local driver (`adapters/local/`), not a copied driver (J316 (a), a two-way door). A row is a small data file in its own folder. It gives the CLI's headless start, its resume by session id, the permission modes the owner may approve and where its login lives. The driver keeps doing everything else the same way: the clone, the approvals, the supervisor, and the stop that ends the whole process tree. A user who has signed in to Pi picks `"harness": "pi"` and gets a fleet builder on Pi.

## Changelog headline

The local driver now runs nine more agent CLIs, each through your own sign-in: Pi, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Goose, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, Qwen Code and Cline CLI.

## User Stories

1. As a Pi (or OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor, Goose, Gemini, Kimi, Qwen or Cline) user, I start a builder on my ticket with that harness, and it uses the login I already have on my machine.
2. As a user, a wake reaches the same agent session: the CLI resumes it by its session id and edits its own status note.
3. As a user, `stop` ends everything the run started, including any background service or hub that the CLI started for it.
4. As an owner, I approve one permission mode per repository and harness, as today, and the driver passes only that mode's fixed arguments from the row.
5. As a row author, I add one folder and touch no shared file. The contract's check tells me exactly what my row breaks.
6. As a reviewer, I can trust a row, because the kit's five checks pass against it on fixtures with a fake CLI that accepts only the real CLI's documented command line.

## Implementation Decisions

- **The contract,** `adapters/local/harness-row.md` (HR1): a row is `adapters/local/harnesses/<harness>/row.json`, read with standard-library JSON, never run as code. Its fields:
  - `harness`: the start field's value, equal to its folder name;
  - `program`: the command found on `PATH`;
  - `start` and `wake`: argument lists, where each placeholder fills a whole argument: `{prompt}`, `{model}`, `{session}` and `{mode}`;
  - `session`: how the driver knows the session id: `{"chosen": "uuid"}` (the driver makes a UUID and passes it at start), `{"json": [<key path>]}` (the first JSON line of the run's output that has that path), or `{"pattern": "<regex with one group>"}`. A session id must match `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,100}` and must not look like a credential by the kit's check;
  - `modes`: each mode value the owner may approve, mapped to the fixed arguments it adds where `{mode}` is;
  - `env`: fixed, non-credential variables the turn gets, such as a CLI's local-backend switch;
  - `login`: one line saying where the CLI's own login lives;
  - `daemon`: `none`, or one line naming the background process the CLI may start and how stop ends it.
- **The driver** (HR1) loads a row only for the harness that a start names. Claude and codex stay built in and unchanged, and no row may use either name. Wake substitutes the saved session id. When a reported id hasn't been seen yet, wake refuses with a D3 error and starts nothing. Stop is unchanged: it ends the whole process tree. Approvals, the fleet.md row per harness, the first-turn watch and the credential check all apply to rows unchanged.
- **The kit check for rows,** `adapters/local/test_harnesses.py` (HR1): for every row folder it checks the row against the contract, then runs `kernel/driver-kit/kit.py` on fixtures with the row's own fake CLI. It needs the kit's five checks, and also: the wake turn got the same session id as the start turn; every `env` value passes the kit's credential check; and the fake's background process, when the row declares one, has ended after stop. The kit's files are not changed.
- **The fake CLI** per row is `harnesses/<harness>/fake`. It is built on the shared library `adapters/local/fixtures/fake_cli.py` (HR1), and it exits 2 on any command line that the real CLI's documentation doesn't allow.
- **Effort (J318):** a user must always be able to set effort. Every row either passes the user's effort to the CLI, through a named flag or setting in its `effort` map, or says plainly in `row.json` and in its README's `Effort:` table line that the host can't set effort. The local driver's `version` lists `effort` in `can`, because claude and codex take it, and carries no per-row note, because its schema is fixed. A start with an effort never silently falls back to a default: a row that can't take it refuses. The `effort` start field comes from driver v1's change in #2471. HR1 builds the row field, the refusal and the runner check below that field, and the runner proves the value reaches the fake CLI's command line or environment.
- **Disjoint rows:** each row ticket owns only `adapters/local/harnesses/<harness>/`. That folder holds `row.json`, `fake`, `README.md` (the login line, the commands, the census check resolved from primary sources, with links), an optional `test_row.py`, which the runner also runs, and `evidence/`. No row edits the driver, the local README, CI or the release lists: `adapters/local/**` is already covered there.
- **Merge gate:** as driver v1 section 3 sets it for any new host, a row merges only after its live check records 5 of 5 at the row pull request's approved head. HR1 merges on fixtures and review, after polish F (#2321), whose approved head it stacks on.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam 1: the contract runner** against planted rows under `adapters/local/fixtures/rows/`, red first. Each planted row must fail with a named reason:
  - a wake with no `{session}`;
  - a placeholder inside a larger argument;
  - a credential in `env`;
  - a background process that survives stop;
  - a fake that is handed a different session id on wake;
  - a row named `claude`;
  - a row that claims effort but never passes it;
  - a row with no effort form.

  One good example row passes.
- **Seam 2: each row** passes the runner with its own fake, red first, against an empty row.
- **Prior art:** `adapters/local/test_driver.py` and its fake harness, and the kit's planted drivers.

## Proof

- **P1 (contract):** the runner's red and green on planted rows, in `adapters/local/evidence/`, plus `test_driver.py` still green.
- **P2 (each row):** its runner pass on fixtures, red first, in the row's `evidence/`. Its README resolves the census check with primary-source links.
- **P3 (stop):** OpenCode's background service and Cline's hub, each simulated by its fake and backed by primary sources, have ended after stop.
- **P4 (live):** each row's live 5-of-5 on a real signed-in CLI, a person's ticket.

## Checkpoints

- One-way door: no
- User-visible: yes

## Live check

For each row, a person signs in to that CLI on their own machine and runs the kit against the local driver with that harness, on one throwaway ticket, at the row pull request's approved head. 5 of 5 is recorded on that pull request.

## Out of Scope

- Copying a driver for each CLI.
- Changing claude's or codex's behaviour.
- Cloud products and daemon-only hosts.
- Harness wave 2, census rows 10 to 15: those are spec #2424, built on this contract.
- Any change to the kit's files.

## Further Notes

The source is the drivers census (private), rows 1 to 9. J316 (a) is the ruling: local CLIs become harness rows on the one local driver, a two-way door. The go is J314.

items.title: 0.1.2 spec: Fleet reliability: merge queue drops and a GraphQL-first read budget
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Two fleet faults were seen live on 2026-11-22.

1. **The merge queue drops a pull request silently.** OpenWiz #2253 was queued with `enqueuePullRequest` at 09:49. At 10:00 GitHub removed it for `branch_protection_failure`, caused by cancelled duplicate changelog runs. Nothing noticed. The planner found it by hand and queued it again at 11:52. Today `merge.py merge` turns a removal at a receipted head into `merge blocked`, and `fleet.sh` then stops printing that merge line, so the drop waits for a person who doesn't know.
2. **REST runs dry.** `fleet.sh` reads each issue's detail, blockers and comments through REST, in 64 parallel lanes. The shared account's REST allowance has run out more than once. GraphQL reads already have an allowance gate (`allowance` in `fleet.sh`); REST has none.

## Solution

- **Queue drops:** on every wake, and right after every enqueue, the fleet reads the queue back. A pull request that is still open and approved at its receipted head but has `isInMergeQueue: false`, or whose timeline holds a `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` after its receipt, is a **drop**. The fleet records it with GitHub's reason, waits while its cause stands, and queues it again once, at the same head, only once the cause is gone. A second drop at the same head is `merge blocked` and goes to the orchestrator: never a loop.
- **Read budget:** the hot reads move to batched GraphQL, and a read budget gates every remaining REST read. It backs off before the allowance runs out, keeping a reserve for builders and reviewers, as the GraphQL gate does today. Every fail-closed rule stays: an unread or unknown answer is never empty.

- **The allowance plan (J320):** the GitHub allowance is the factory's top limit. The target after the bench is **100 agents under 3,000 REST calls an hour**, on one account; extra accounts to multiply the allowance are not allowed. In order: measure the spenders first (BEFORE bench); read files and branches from git, not the API; make every repeated poll conditional (`If-None-Match`, a `304` costs no primary allowance); read each repository once per wake into a snapshot that started agents read; do wide reads in one GraphQL query per spec; and pace writes under GitHub's secondary limits (about 80 content-creating requests a minute, 500 an hour, 100 concurrent).

## Changelog headline

none

## User Stories

1. As a fleet owner, a pull request GitHub drops from the merge queue is noticed on the next wake, with GitHub's reason on the pull request, and goes back in once its cause is gone.
2. As a fleet owner, a pull request that drops twice at one head stops and asks the orchestrator, so the fleet never re-queues in a loop.
3. As a fleet owner running many fleets on one account, a fleet wake backs off before the REST allowance is gone instead of failing every check until it resets.

## Implementation Decisions

- **The drop decider** is a new script, `skills/launch-fleet/scripts/queue.py` in `openwizdev/WizSkills` (FR1). It reads one pull request's queue facts by GraphQL (state, head, `isInMergeQueue`, `mergeQueueEntry`, the latest `AddedToMergeQueueEvent` and `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent`, the head's required checks) and the record author's `merge queued` / `merge dropped` records, and prints one verdict: `queued`, `merged <commit>`, `dropped <commit>: <reason>` (a new drop to record), `wait <commit>: <cause>` (the cause stands), `requeue <commit>: <why the cause is gone>`, or `blocked <commit>: dropped twice`. It only reads.
- **Cause gone, by reason:** `branch_protection_failure` and `failed_checks`: every required check's latest run on the head is green and none is running, and the removal is older than those runs or its failed runs were cancelled duplicates; `merge_conflict`: never automatic (builder merges `main` in, new head, new review as today); `dequeued`/manual removal by a person: never automatic; an unknown reason: never automatic. Unreadable facts are `wait`, never `requeue`.
- **The record:** `launch-fleet: merge dropped <commit>: <reason>` on the pull request, once per removal event. One automatic re-queue per head, counted from those records.
- **Wiring** (FR2): `merge.py merge` calls the decider where it now blocks on `it left the queue`, re-reads the queue after every enqueue, and records the drop and the re-queue itself. `fleet.sh` keeps printing the merge line while a drop waits, so every wake re-reads it.
- **The read budget** is a new script, `skills/launch-fleet/scripts/budget.py` in `openwizdev/WizSkills` (FR3): it reads REST's `x-ratelimit-*` headers of the latest reads (and `/rate_limit`, which costs nothing) and admits or refuses the next batch of N reads, keeping a quarter of the hour's allowance for builders and reviewers. Exit 0 admits, 1 backs off with the reset time, 2 is unknown, which also refuses.
- **The move** (FR4): issue detail, blockers and comments are read in batched GraphQL queries (many issues per query, paged comments to the end), with REST kept only where GraphQL has no equivalent, each REST batch through the budget. It builds on #2376's repository-keyed closing-PR reads.

- **The allowance tickets:** FR5 the meter and BEFORE bench (`gh-meter.py`); FR6 `gitread.py` (default-branch file reads from a fetched cache; `post.py` and `ops-starts.py` first); FR7 `ghcache.py` (ETag conditional GETs for Python callers; `fleet.sh` already revalidates its own REST reads); FR8 `snapshot.py` (one GraphQL read of a repository's open issues, pull requests and comments per wake); FR9 the wide reads of `fleet.sh` in GraphQL (FR4 keeps the per-issue reads); FR10 a write pacer in `post.py`, every record's one writer; FR11 `status.py` on FR6 and FR7; FR12 briefs carry the snapshot's facts. Each helper is a new file, so most of these build at once.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam 1:** `queue.py` against fixtures of real GraphQL answers: #2253's drop (`branch_protection_failure` after cancelled duplicate runs), a drop with checks still red, a merge conflict, a person's removal, a second drop at one head, an unreadable answer. Red first.
- **Seam 2:** `test-merge.py` through `merge.py merge` with the fake `gh`: drop, wait, re-queue once, second drop blocks.
- **Seam 3:** `budget.py` on header fixtures: plenty, near the reserve, empty, missing headers. And `test.sh`: a check whose REST allowance is near the reserve backs off with exit 2 and no partial facts; the GraphQL batch reads give the same facts as today's REST reads on the existing fixtures.

## Proof

- **P1** (drops): `test-merge.py` and `queue.py`'s tests, red first, including #2253's replayed answers.
- **P2** (budget): `budget.py`'s tests and the new `test.sh` cases, red first, and the REST reads per `fleet.sh spec` run counted before and after on the same fixture.

- **P3** (allowance): FR5's BEFORE table, with the top five spenders, and an AFTER run of the same bench once the others land, against the 3,000-an-hour target.

## Checkpoints

- One-way door: yes
- User-visible: no

## Out of Scope

- Cross-repository closing-PR reads: #2376 (in progress, openwizdev/WizSkills#284). Related; this spec owns none of its lines, and FR4 waits for it.
- Cost reviewer records by full PR identity: #2375 (polish Y, #2387, openwizdev/WizSkills#281). Related; this spec owns none of its lines, and FR2 waits for it.
- The changelog workflow's duplicate runs themselves.
- More GitHub accounts to multiply the allowance (not allowed).
- The orchestrator's own private watch loop: it adopts FR7's helper privately, outside this spec.

## Further Notes

Seen live on 2026-11-22: OpenWiz #2253 (dropped 10:00, re-queued by hand 11:52) and the REST runs out on the shared account. The planner's go: J314; widened under J320.

items.title: 0.1.2 spec: Marketplace v0, a public registry and openwiz.dev/market
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Everything that plugs into OpenWiz (drivers, harnesses, skills, and anything else in the agent economy) is scattered across pull requests, a hand-written Drivers page and the WizSkills README. Nobody outside the org can say "I built one, list it", and a reader can't tell which pieces were proven on a real host and which are only claims. OpenWiz grows with its network: every listing makes the next user more likely to come, so publishing must be open to anyone.

## Solution

A public registry repository, `openwizdev/WizMarket`, holds one small file per listing, added by pull request by anyone. The publisher tags what the listing is with their own tags; kinds are tags, not a list we own. Each listing says `listed` or `verified`, and WizMarket's CI accepts `verified` only with the right proof for its kind: a saved five-check kit receipt from the real host for a driver or harness, or the skill's own check passing at a pinned version for a skill. Any other `verified` claim is refused. **openwiz.dev/market** is generated from the registry at build time: no server, no accounts, no payments. It opens seeded with the three shipped drivers, the drivers and harnesses being built (as `listed`, with their pull request or ticket) and the WizSkills skills. The Drivers page reads the same registry, so the two can't disagree.

## Changelog headline

Anyone can now list what they built for OpenWiz on openwiz.dev/market, tagged however they choose, and it shows as verified once it passes its test.

## User Stories

1. As anyone with a GitHub account, I add one file to WizMarket by pull request and my listing appears on openwiz.dev/market after review and merge.
2. As a publisher, I tag my listing with what it is, in my own words (`driver`, `mcp-server`, `sandbox`, anything), and readers can browse by tag.
3. As a reader, I see at a glance whether a listing is `verified` (proven by its kind's test) or `listed` (a link, not proven), and I can open the proof.
4. As a driver or harness author, I add my kit receipt from the real host and CI accepts my `verified` listing; without it, CI refuses the claim and tells me to drop to `listed`.
5. As a skill author, I pin my skill's source at a commit and name its check; CI runs that check at that commit and accepts `verified` only when it passes.
6. As a reader of openwiz.dev/drivers, I see the same drivers, states and proofs as the market, because both pages are built from one registry snapshot.
7. As a publisher, the pull request template and one paragraph on the market page tell me exactly how to publish.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Contract first** (MK1): `contracts/listing.v1.md` in `openwizdev/WizMarket`, with `schema/listing.v1.json` and synthetic examples in `fixtures/`. Everything else builds on it in parallel.
- **A listing** is `listings/<id>.json`, standard-library JSON. `id` is the file's name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 40 characters. Fields: `name`, `summary` (one line, at most 140 characters), `tags` (1 to 8 publisher-chosen tags, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), `url` (https), `plugs_into` (one line: what in OpenWiz it plugs into), `publisher` (a GitHub login), `stage` (`available` or `being-built`; `being-built` needs a `links` entry to its public pull request or ticket), optional `login` (one line, where the login lives, as the Drivers page says it), optional `links` (label and https URL), `status` (`listed` or `verified`) and `proof` (required when `verified`, absent otherwise). No other field.
- **Verified by kind,** decided from the tags:
  - tag `driver` or `harness`: `proof` is `{"receipt": "receipts/<id>/<file>.txt"}`. The receipt is plain text: header lines `# listing: <id>`, `# host: <real host>`, `# driver: <owner/repo>@<40-hex commit>`, `# kit: openwizdev/OpenWiz@<40-hex commit>`, `# harness: <harness>`, `# model: <model>`, `# date: <YYYY-MM-DD>`, `# run by: <the GitHub login whose gh the kit read with>`, then kit.py's stdout verbatim: the five lines `pass version: ...`, `pass start: ...`, `pass wake: ...`, `pass stop: ...`, `pass token: ...` in that order, and `Result: 5 of 5 pass`. The pull request that adds a receipt is its public record; the throwaway repository and ticket never appear.
  - tag `skill`: `proof` is `{"source": "<owner/repo>@<40-hex commit>", "check": "<command>"}`. CI checks out that exact commit and runs the command there, in a job with no secrets and read-only permissions, with a time limit; exit 0 is a pass.
  - any other tags: `verified` is refused; the listing is `listed`.
  - A listing tagged both `driver` and `skill` needs both proofs.
- **The check** (MK2): `check/check.py` in `openwizdev/WizMarket`, Python 3.11 standard library. `check` validates every listing, receipt and fixture against the contract and a privacy scan (no token shapes, private ids or machine paths), and exits 1 naming each failure; `index` prints the registry index, the contract's one shape for consumers: the registry's commit and every listing with its checked status, its receipt's date and public URL when verified. `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs `check` on every pull request and push, and runs a skill's check only for skill listings the pull request adds or changes.
- **The market page** (MK8): `market/index.html` in `openwizdev/WizSite`, generated by `build.mjs` from `market/registry.json`, a pinned snapshot of WizMarket's `index` output, refreshed by `scripts/market-sync.mjs <WizMarket checkout>`, so the build needs no network. Static: listing cards with name, summary, tags, status and stage, browsable by tag without a server. It carries the one "Publish your own" paragraph, linking WizMarket's template.
- **One source** (MK9): the Drivers page's driver cards and "being built" list come from the same `market/registry.json` (listings tagged `driver`), generated at build time; the page's hand-written sections (the explainer, the key-host section from #2380, "write your own driver") stay hand-written. Coordinated with KY3 (#2380) and the Drivers page keeper, who also edit `drivers/index.html`.
- **Seeds** (MK4 to MK7), one batch per kind, all in WizMarket: the three shipped drivers (`local`, `boat-dev`, `cloudroom`) as `verified` with receipts faithfully converted from their recorded public kit runs; the drivers and harnesses being built as `listed`, `being-built`, each with its pull request or ticket link; the WizSkills skills as `verified` at the pinned WizSkills release commit where `python3 check/run.py --shard <skill>` passes there, `listed` otherwise.
- **Publish your own** (MK3): `.github/pull_request_template.md` and the README's publish section in WizMarket.
- **Final refresh** (MK10): once the seeds and the check merge, WizSite's snapshot is synced from WizMarket main.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam 1: WizMarket's check on fixtures.** `check/test_check.py` runs `check.py` against valid and broken fixture listings and receipts: a false `verified` for each kind is refused, a 4-of-5 receipt is refused, a receipt naming another listing is refused, a skill check that fails at its commit is refused, an unknown field is refused, and `index` prints the contract's shape. Red first.
- **Seam 2: the real registry in CI.** Every seed pull request goes green under the merged check; a skill listing's check really runs at its pinned commit.
- **Seam 3: the built site.** WizSite's tests build `dist/` from a fixture snapshot and from the real one: `/market/` lists every listing with its status, tags and links; the Drivers page's driver cards match the registry's `driver` listings exactly.
- **Prior art:** WizSite's `scripts/changelog.mjs` (a page generated from data files at build time) and `tests/drivers.test.mjs`; WizSkills' `check/run.py --shard`; OpenWiz's `kernel/driver-kit/kit.py` output.

## Proof

- **P1** (contract): `contracts/listing.v1.md`, its schema and fixtures, reviewed against this spec.
- **P2** (check): `check/test_check.py` red then green in CI; a false `verified` refused on a real pull request.
- **P3** (seeds): each seed pull request green under the check; skill listings verified only where their check passed at the pinned commit.
- **P4** (market): the built `/market/` page's test, and a preview link for the owner's late look.
- **P5** (one source): the Drivers page test proves its driver cards equal the registry's.
- **P6** (publish): the template and paragraph, reviewed for a first-time publisher.

## Checkpoints

- One-way door: yes
- User-visible: yes

## Live check

none: nothing touches a user's machine or account. The owner's late look is a preview of openwiz.dev/market before the final WizSite merge.

## Out of Scope

- Payments, paid listings, accounts or any server (a later grill, with the business-model questions).

items.title: 0.1.2 spec: Effort everywhere: every driver passes the user's effort, or says plainly it can't
items.body:
## Problem Statement

A user sets each role's effort in `docs/agents/fleet.md`'s Models table (Medium for OpenWiz today), just as they set its model. But driver v1's `start` carries only `repository`, `ticket`, `skill`, `harness` and `model`. So any agent started through a driver runs at its host's default effort, whatever the user set. The CloudRoom driver spawns with `--provider` and `--model` and no `--reasoning-level`. The local driver runs `claude` and `codex` with no effort flag. The boat.dev driver uses boat's default effort. Nothing says so at start time. Once a project has a `## Roster` (KN21, openwizdev/WizSkills#262), every Roster start goes through a driver, so every one of them would quietly drop the user's effort.

## Solution

Effort becomes a first-class setting, like the model (J318). A driver either passes the user's effort to its host, or says plainly that the host can't set it: `effort` is absent from `version`'s `can`, its README has an `Effort:` line, and it refuses with one fixed D3 text. No start silently falls back to a default when the user set an effort: the start carries it, or it is refused and nothing starts. launch-fleet's Roster path sends the effort from the Models table to drivers that take it, and refuses to start through one that can't. Harness rows on the local driver follow the same rule through HR1 (#2431).

## Changelog headline

You can always set effort: every driver passes your effort to its host, or says plainly that it can't, and never starts at a default when you set one.

## User Stories

1. As a user who sets Medium effort for builders, every builder started through the CloudRoom driver runs at Medium (`room-cli thread spawn --reasoning-level medium`).
2. As a user on the local driver, `claude` and `codex` builders run at the effort I set, through each CLI's own effort option.
3. As a user on boat.dev, the driver either passes my effort, or tells me plainly that boat.dev runs at its own default effort.
4. As a user with a Roster, launch-fleet sends my configured effort to the picked driver, and if that driver can't run my harness at that effort, the ticket isn't started and its fleet line says why.
5. As a driver author, the kit tells me whether my driver passes effort to its host, or says plainly that it can't.
6. As a user of any driver that can't set effort, I can tell three ways:
   - `effort` is missing from its `version` `can` list;
   - one `Effort:` line under its README's login line says so;
   - a start with an effort is refused with a `next` that tells me what to change.

## Implementation Decisions

**The contract (driver v1, additive).** No v1 rule's meaning changes. `kernel/driver.v1.md` gains these, and `kernel/driver-kit/schema.json` their shapes:

- **`effort` in `start`.** An optional `start` input field: one plain word, `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,19}$`, as the user wrote it in lower case (for example `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`). The other five fields stay required as they are.
- **`effort` in `can`.** `version`'s `can` may list `effort`. A caller sends `effort` only to a driver whose `can` lists it. A driver that doesn't list it is never sent the field, and still refuses it under D1, exactly as today.
- **`version`'s answer is unchanged except for that `can` entry.** It carries no effort note: every answer matches its schema exactly (D1). A driver says it can't set effort in exactly three ways:
  - `effort` is absent from its `can` list;
  - a plain `Effort:` line in its README;
  - the D3 refusal below.
- **The refusal text.** A driver that can't set the effort it was sent, for the start's harness, refuses (D3) with `next` exactly: `this host can't set effort: remove the effort for this harness in your Models table or Roster to run it at the host's default`. Its `error` names the harness and the effort word.
- **E1. Passed or refused.** A driver whose `can` lists `effort` runs the host at exactly the start's effort, for every harness and value its README lists as passed. Its README names the exact flag or setting. For any other harness or value, it refuses with the refusal text above and starts nothing. It never substitutes a nearby value and never falls back to a default.
- **E2. No effort, host default.** A `start` without `effort` runs at the host's default effort. That is the case where the user set none.
- **E3. It says so.** Right under its login line, every driver's README has one `Effort:` line: `Effort: passed as <flag or setting>` or `Effort: the host can't set it (<why>)`. When it differs by harness, a short table of harness, flag or `can't (<why>)` follows. A driver that can't set effort for any harness leaves `effort` out of `can`. It is never sent the field, and refuses it under D1 as today.
- **E4. Callers never drop it.** When the user set an effort for a role, a caller sends it only to a driver whose `can` lists `effort`. Through any other driver, it starts nothing. A refusal with the refusal text above also starts nothing. A caller never retries without the effort.

**Expand, then contract.** EF1 adds the fields. EF2 adds the kit's `effort` check, which at first lets a driver that neither lists `effort` in `can` nor has a README `Effort:` line pass with a note. Each driver then declares its effort. Last, EF14 makes the declaration required. So main stays green at every merge, and a driver still in flight takes one small follow-up. Because every driver's `schema` must print `schema.json` unchanged, EF1 also updates every `adapters/*/schema.json` copy on main in the same pull request.

**The kit's `effort` check.** It is part of the existing `start` check, not a sixth check: the kit still prints five lines, so "5 of 5" and the write-driver contract stay true. A failed effort part fails `start`.
- **A driver whose `can` lists `effort`:** the kit's start carries `effort` (`--effort <v>`, default `medium`).
  - It passes when that value appears in the command line or environment of a process the run started (the kit already watches these for the token check), or, for a key-host driver, in the request its loopback fake host received (the log KY1's key check uses). That is what a host CLI, `room-cli` or a host API receives.
  - It also passes when the start is refused with exactly the refusal text, with no run, and the README's `Effort:` line or table says that harness can't.
- **A driver without `effort` in `can`:** it passes only when a start with `effort` is refused (D1) with no run, and the README's `Effort:` line says the host can't set it.
- **A planted driver that lists effort but never passes it:** fails.

**The drivers.**
- **CloudRoom:** `effort` becomes `--reasoning-level <effort>`, for the providers `room-cli thread spawn --help` accepts it for. Any other provider gets the refusal text.
- **Local:** effort goes to `claude --effort <level>` and to `codex exec -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>`, each checked against that CLI's own `--help`. Harness rows use HR1's effort hook (#2431).
- **boat.dev:** it passes effort if `boat prompt` has a documented option for it. Otherwise it leaves `effort` out of `can`, and its README says boat.dev runs use the host's default effort (DW10).
- **Template:** it shows the passing form, so a copied driver starts from the rule.

**launch-fleet (in openwizdev/WizSkills).**
- **Starts through the Roster:** `host.py start` reads the role's Effort cell from the Models table and the driver's `version` `can`.
  - When an effort is set and `can` lists `effort`, the start carries it.
  - When an effort is set and `can` doesn't list it, nothing starts.
  - When the driver refuses with the refusal text, nothing is started.
  - Either way, the fleet line reads `stopped (driver can't set effort)`.
  - When no effort is set, the start is unchanged.
- **Starts without a Roster:** unchanged.
- **Where it builds:** this work builds on KN21's head (openwizdev/WizSkills#262) and merges into that pull request's branch, so KN21 reaches main with effort.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seam 1, the kit:** `kernel/driver-kit/test_kit.py` runs the template, planted drivers and the new effort fixtures. Red first: a planted driver that lists effort but drops it must fail `start`.
- **Seam 2, each driver:** its `test_driver.py` on its synthetic host CLI. Red first, the start with `effort: medium` must reach the fake CLI's arguments: `room-cli … --reasoning-level medium`, `claude … --effort medium`, `codex exec … -c model_reasoning_effort=medium`. A harness or value the driver can't set is refused with exactly the refusal text, and nothing starts.
- **Seam 3, launch-fleet:** `test-host.py` starts a ticket through a Roster entry on a fake driver whose `can` lists effort, and the driver receives `"effort": "medium"`. A driver without it in `can`, or one that answers the refusal text, gets no start, and the line is `stopped (driver can't set effort)`.
- **Prior art:** the kit's token check (process command lines and environments), the drivers' fake CLIs, and KN21's Roster fixtures.

## Proof

| Claim | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| The contract is additive | EF1's diff touches no v1 rule's text, and every existing driver test stays green on the new schema |
| The kit sees effort reach the host, or the plain statement | EF2's planted drivers, red then green |
| CloudRoom, local and the template pass effort | each driver's fixture test, red then green, plus the effort part of the kit's `start` check |
| boat.dev passes it or says it can't | its fixture test and README, plus the effort part of the kit's `start` check |
| Roster starts carry effort, or refuse | launch-fleet's `test-host.py`, red then green |
| No driver on main is silent | EF14: the kit requires the README `Effort:` line, and every `adapters/*/` passes it |

## Checkpoints

- One-way door: yes
- User-visible: yes

## Live check

On the CloudRoom driver, one throwaway ticket started through a Roster entry with Medium effort. The spawned thread's reasoning level reads `medium`. It is recorded on EF7's pull request.

## Out of Scope

- The harness-row effort rule and its kit runner: HR1 (#2431) owns it, and this spec only fixes the field it builds to.
- Driver v2, and any change to a v1 rule's meaning.
- Changing a wave-1 driver's frozen head before its live run and merge (#2017, #2018, #2020, #2021, #2022, #2029): each one gets its own follow-up ticket here.
- Other in-flight drivers' effort work: each one's own spec adds it.

## Further Notes

This spec replaces this issue's original follow-up body. That body came from KN23 (#1856, draft PR #2465) built on KN21 (#1854, openwizdev/WizSkills#262): Roster starts dropped the Models table's effort, and the CloudRoom driver had no `--reasoning-level`. J318 (private record) is the ruling, and it makes effort first-class for every driver.

**Holds:**
- KN21 (openwizdev/WizSkills#262) merges once EF7 has merged into its branch.
- KN23 (#2465) waits for KN21, EF3 and EF7.
- #2488 (Roster-first reviews) is a sibling and is unchanged.
